subject.title: cron: startup catch-up deferral lost on a second restart before it fires (silent missed run)

question: Which open fix path should be treated as canonical for persisting startup catch-up deferral markers across restarts?
rationale: Both open PRs reference this issue with closing syntax, but they use different storage boundaries and current review comments identify different merge blockers; choosing the canonical branch is a maintainer/storage-boundary decision.

options.title: Use the SQLite-backed state path
options.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102292 once its cron read-response compatibility blocker is fixed, because it keeps the marker with the cron runtime state instead of adding a new sidecar.

options.title: Ask the sidecar PR to rework storage
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102874 open only if it is revised to SQLite-owned marker persistence or a storage owner explicitly accepts the sidecar tradeoff.

options.title: Pause until a storage owner chooses
options.body: Keep this issue and both PRs open while a cron/storage owner decides the permanent internal marker shape.

recommendation.title: Use the SQLite-backed state path
recommendation.body: Prefer https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102292 once its cron read-response compatibility blocker is fixed, because it keeps the marker with the cron runtime state instead of adding a new sidecar.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron storage-boundary review context and current-area history make this the best available owner for choosing between SQLite-owned state and sidecar persistence.
